label: CONSERVED_FUNCTIONAL_BENCHMARK_v2
what: Six ACCUMULATION boards whose conserved replacement is already known. A proposer sees the before-board and its leak, never the after-board, and is scored on whether it names the functional that worked -- or one an adversary cannot kill.
why_six: These are every ACCUMULATION item in the corpus (5) plus the trio's K1 -> K3, which is the exemplar the taxonomy was induced from. Six is small. It is six more than a pipeline with no benchmark has.
blinding: The proposer is given: state, move, invariant, composition and the leak sentence. It is NOT given the after-board, the paper, the year, or the names. The recognition probe from the protocol tree applies -- ask it to name the problem, and record the answer, because D25 measured that a rater who recognises the problem needs no rule.

scoring.primary: THE TWO DISCRIMINATORS, not board-discovery. T1: can the invariant be verified on the STARTING STATE by an independent computation, without knowing whether the theorem is true? T2: is the legal move a formula, or does it need an existence theorem?

T1_examples.Guo-Fang-Lu: YES -- Lemma 2.4 is three lines of calculus plus a gamma integral, checkable on the seed with the conjecture's truth unknown
T1_examples.Banaszczyk: YES -- the Gaussian measure of a body is computable
T1_examples.Bansal-Jiang: YES, but only via an SDP feasibility THEOREM, which is why it also fails T2

T2_examples.Bansal-Jiang: existence theorem (SDP duality, Thm 2.12) -- most of the complexity difference between the two papers
T2_examples.Banaszczyk: EXISTENCE THEOREM -- corrected by the control runs, which killed both formula readings: K intersect (K-v) is legal but loses measure (slab 0.68 -> 0.5035, shifted 0.2 and intersected -> 0.3688), and conv((K+v) union (K-v)) keeps the measure but is not a SUBSET of the union. The move needs a lemma whose iteration IS the theorem. My prediction said formula and was wrong.

scoring.secondary: does the proposer itself say whether its candidate relocates or removes the obstruction
scoring.not_applicable: declines. A first-class number, not a footnote.
scoring.what_is_NOT_scored: whether the board is 'a board change' rather than 'a better player'. The audit is right that this framing should go: affine spectral independence IS a board change by any definition that admits Odin's. CHECKABILITY is the discriminator, not board-change-versus-not.
scoring.T3: ADDED BY THE CONTROL RUNS. Evaluate the invariant's threshold on the TARGET state: min{C : invariant holds at scale C}. T1 and T2 both pass on Banaszczyk's board, which is capped at Theta(sqrt log n) by this computation alone, so the two original discriminators are not sufficient.

items.degrading: Gaussian measure of a symmetric convex body stays >= 1/2, and degrades under each application of the move
items.move: replace the body by a convex subset of the union of its two translates
items.conserved_answer: directional total variation of a density supported on the body, preserved exactly under the move

items.degrading: density increment delta -> delta + c delta^2 over about 1/delta iterations, each costing one dimension
items.move: large Fourier coefficient, then restrict to a hyperplane
items.conserved_answer: slice rank -- a one-shot bound with no iteration at all

items.degrading: matrix Chernoff on E||Sigma_S||; the factor n in tr exp gives log n, tight on direct sums of independent blocks
items.conserved_answer: the largest root of the expected characteristic polynomial: for a direct sum it is the MAXIMUM over blocks, so the bound is dimension-free

items.degrading: per-set Chernoff bound composed by a union bound over n sets, which is where the sqrt(log n) comes from
items.conserved_answer: entropy of a partial colouring -- a global count that does not pay per set

items.degrading: a recursive inequality on J where each iteration recovers a fixed fraction of the defect, so about log k rounds are needed
items.conserved_answer: efficient congruencing: maintain congruence conditions at every scale simultaneously, removing the accumulation over rounds

items.degrading: value decay under k-fold repetition, with instance size multiplicative in the exponent (n^k)
items.conserved_answer: graph powering on expanders plus alphabet reduction, with constant-factor size blow-up

items.degrading: n/a -- this item is the negative control, not a board
items.move: convolution with a class closed under it
items.conserved_answer: NONE EXISTS THAT IS CHECKABLE: the class exists iff Komlos holds, so any invariant for it is equivalent to the conjecture. Correct answer: decline, and say why.
items.scores_as: T1 fails. A proposer that offers this board as a find has produced a restatement.

not_runnable_here: No ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and no model access in this container -- the same wall as debt D18. The harness to run it exists at proof-protocol/p2-ablation/, fidelity-tested against the published artifact's own JavaScript.
first_thing_to_check_when_it_runs: the recognition probe. If a proposer names the problem, D25 applies and a hit tells you nothing about the screen -- it tells you the model remembers Ellenberg-Gijswijt. The only uncontaminated items would be boards whose transformation does not exist yet, which is why FINDER.md section 4 points at 2609.11189's own three open leaks.
superseded_v1: v1 scored a proposer on whether it named the historical conserved functional. The audit's objection kills that metric outright: 4 of 4 models found a composable invariant and 0 of 4 found a CHECKABLE one, so the experiment as stated would score 100% and measure nothing.

positive.why: a real board with a checkable invariant: gamma of a body is computable, the terminal condition is a theorem, and it reaches sqrt(log n). A rubric that cannot pass this is not measuring board-finding.

negative.what: the board all four models converged on: a class C closed under convolution with the terminal property.
negative.why_it_is_a_trap: one of them proved that such a class exists if and only if Komlos holds, and reported it as a finding when it is the diagnosis. CORRECTED BY THE CONTROL RUN: the respondent declines the iff -- closure implies Komlos by unwinding, but the converse is not automatic, so this is a restatement-OR-STRONGER, a possibly-stronger certificate scheme rather than a literal logical restatement. The trap works either way, since the invariant still cannot be checked on the starting state until the class is named; but the reference corpus's 'if and only if' is now the claim needing a check.
negative.why_it_fixes_the_benchmark: this is the first negative control in the programme that RECALL CANNOT CRACK. D25 measured that a rule-less rater ceilings the retrospective arm at J = 1.000 with 13/13 recognition, because naming the problem is enough. An invariant equivalent to the theorem is not a famous problem to remember -- it is a generic trap, and telling it apart from Banaszczyk requires the computation rather than the memory.
negative.input_defect: the input as written said 'a class of SYMMETRIC convex bodies'. The gluing lemma's bodies are not symmetric and symmetry cannot be restored: with K = B_2 and v = e_1 the translates are externally tangent at 0, the union contains no ball around 0, so every symmetric convex subset is gamma-null. Caught by the respondent; fix the input before reuse.

contamination: Withholding the paper does not work with tools: both tool-enabled models found the surrounding literature within minutes, and one retrieved three real arXiv ids with zero fabrications. Either run tools-off, or run a tool-enabled arm PURELY to measure contamination. The recognition probe is read first either way.
